analysis.title: Rates Forecast Update – More hikes to come
key_insights: RBC sees central banks in inflation-fighting mode to avoid second-round effects from energy prices. The RBA was first to hike and is probably done, the ECB has one more hike to come, the BoE should follow its November hike with another, and the Fed probably hikes at least two more times.
The BoC has a lot of room before reaching a restrictive setting. RBC expects a December hike and a 3.25% terminal rate, with risks leaning to more hikes.
Bond yields are off their peak but could be biased higher near term if equity markets stabilize. Once tightening cycles are advanced or finished, yields should edge slightly lower.

The UK is the main exception: the market prices significantly more tightening (~90bp of hikes, about three more via forward SONIA) than RBC thinks is possible, setting up Gilt absolute and relative outperformance.

Fed: RBC still expects 25bp hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027. It sees a relatively high probability of back-to-back hikes in Dec/Jan and/or a quarterly pace beyond March. The probability the Fed stops short of removing the remaining 50bp of 'insurance cuts' from last year is very low.

Even a lasting Iran ceasefire is unlikely to change RBC's base case of two more Fed hikes, because energy-related inflation pressure stays in the pipeline and energy prices may not fall immediately alongside crude.

US yields overshot lower on the retracement from post-September FOMC highs amid cracks in AI and broader risk sentiment. Hot NFP and CPI reports and Fed rhetoric pushed yields back to fairer levels. RBC sees them biased higher through Q1 2027, modestly lower in Q2 as the Fed holds, then modestly higher in H2 as Treasury begins coupon supply increases.
RBC US forecast: 10y at 5.00% now, 5.05% Q4-26, 5.10% Q1-27, 5.00% Q2-27, 5.05% Q3-27. Policy rate goes from 3.88% to 4.38% by Q1-27.

Canada: the BoC hiked in October with hawkish comments from Macklem. GDP growth forecasts were raised for 2026-2028. RBC expects a December hike to reach the middle of the 2.25-3.25% neutral range, then two more hikes to 3.25%. Universally softer data (Oct CPI, Q3 GDP, Nov jobs) could derail a December hike.

CORRA futures price the 3.25% terminal rate by end-2027, two quarters later than RBC's Q2 timing. RBC sees upside potential for Canadian yields, possible further curve flattening, and possible CAD rate underperformance versus US rates.

ECB: rates held at 2.5% in October. RBC sees one more hike in December as very likely, then a pause with a 2.75% terminal rate. Further hikes depend on second-round effects through wages, which the ECB sees little sign of so far.

Bund yields rallied strongly over the past month on growth concerns and lower energy prices. France looks fiscally precarious, with a narrow political path to the needed budget cuts. RBC expects a dip in Bund yields over the next couple of months, a slight rise in H2 2027, and steeper curves into 2027 as higher term premia reassert.

UK: the BoE hiked 25bp in early November, more hawkish than expected. Mann voted for 50bp, and Bailey said more tightening is needed unless the Middle East energy situation changes dramatically. RBC now expects another 25bp in February, then a long hold.
RBC leaves its UK yield forecasts unchanged: 2y 4.93% now, 4.75% Q4-26, 4.10% Q3-27. The UK budget did not scare markets on fiscal risk, and RBC sees no need for a substantial term premium increase.

Australia: the RBA hiked to a post-GFC high of 4.85% on a 6-3 split vote with balanced forward guidance, so RBC thinks it is at terminal. Only about 4bp of further hikes are priced, then roughly one cut by end-2027. RBC's base case is no move until a cut in November 2027, though it sees the risk of one more hike by mid-2027 as somewhat underpriced.
RBC favors paying Feb and May-27 OIS in Australia against core longs in 1-5y rates, and expects curves to steepen into year-end. October CPI (25 Nov) and Q4 CPI (27 Jan) are the key data.
Cross-market: RBC forecasts the UST-Gilt 10y spread moving from -25bp to +10bp in Q1-27, and the UST-Bund 10y spread widening from 166bp to 190bp in Q1-27.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish MPC with Mann voting for 50bp, Bailey saying more tightening is required, and the chief economist implying a further hike before Christmas. Forward SONIA implies about three more hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: RBC thinks BoE communication suggests there should not be a hiking cycle. After two 25bp hikes from an already restrictive base, the BoE should hold for a long time. Market pricing of ~90bp is too steep.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Second-round effects, meaning higher wage growth, materializing, or the Middle East energy situation changing dramatically.

tension_points.bull_case: Stable labor markets, problematic inflation data with upside risks, and hot NFP and CPI reports support hikes in Dec and Mar, possibly back-to-back or a quarterly pace beyond March.
tension_points.bear_case: Further equity declines, an AI-related growth slowdown, financial stability or contagion risks, or a lasting Iran ceasefire could lead the market to price a skipped December hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further equity declines that hit the real economy through the wealth effect or slower AI-related growth, or financial stability and contagion risks.

tension_points.bull_case: RBC sees the risk of one more hike by mid next year as somewhat underpriced, with hot October and Q4 CPI prints as the trigger.
tension_points.bear_case: The RBA is probably at terminal, the 6-3 split vote and balanced guidance were dovish, and it signaled a pause to 'take stock'.
tension_points.what_invalidates: October CPI (due 25 Nov) and Q4 CPI (27 Jan) coming in hot would require hike pricing for Feb through May to lift.
